title: The prince’s tune, lingering and striding
question: Why does the same violin melody seem to linger with Stokowski and stride with Monteux?
intro: Two violin sections begin the young lovers’ movement of Scheherazade, singing in G major above held lower strings. Stokowski’s Philadelphia players slide between notes and take their time over the tune. Monteux’s San Francisco orchestra keeps it moving, with a brisker step beneath the long phrases.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra
recordings.note: Broad phrases and audible slides between string notes give the melody a singing, unhurried warmth.

recordings.label: Pierre Monteux, San Francisco Symphony
recordings.note: Monteux presses ahead through the lovers’ music, keeping the beat moving beneath the violins’ long phrases.

passages.label: The violins’ long tune
passages.note: Both violin sections sing together. Long notes open into little runs above the held chords of the lower strings.

passages.label: Quick notes within the phrase
passages.note: The violins curl through quick notes, then settle back onto the melody’s longer ones. The lower strings keep their quiet support.

passages.label: The strings swell
passages.note: The violin phrase grows fuller and more emphatic, then eases back as the melody continues.
